hero.headline: White House to sign framework for Iran peace deal Sunday
hero.body:
President Trump announced Saturday that the United States plans to sign a peace framework with Iran on Sunday, capping weeks of negotiations between the two countries. The announcement comes as the administration seeks to reshape relations with Tehran after years of tension between Washington and the Iranian government.

Trump wrote on Truth Social that the deal is scheduled to be signed and described the current relationship with Iran as better than what previous administrations achieved. He expressed hope that the process will work out successfully. The framework represents a significant shift in US policy toward Iran, though specific details of the agreement have not been disclosed publicly.

The impending deal has drawn criticism from some Democrats in Congress. Representative Seth Moulton of Massachusetts called the reported terms a terrible deal and characterized it as a surrender document from Trump to Iran's supreme leader. His comments on MS NOW reflected concerns among some lawmakers about the substance of the negotiations and what concessions may have been made to reach an agreement.

Interior Secretary Doug Burgum defended the administration's approach to Iran on Friday, though he focused his remarks on domestic energy policy rather than the diplomatic negotiations. The signing comes at a time when gas prices have become a point of political contention, with Burgum attributing price variations to state policies rather than international factors.

The Iran framework marks one of the most significant foreign policy developments of Trump's current term. The Sunday signing will formalize a new direction in US-Iran relations, though the agreement will likely face scrutiny from Congress and require implementation steps before its full impact becomes clear. The deal stands in contrast to the Obama-era nuclear agreement, which Trump has criticized repeatedly.

cards.headline: Ebola Outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo Kills at Least 140
cards.teaser: Aid agencies are rushing assistance to health workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo as an Ebola outbreak spreads.
cards.body:
At least 140 people have died from Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo, though aid agencies warn the true toll may be significantly higher. The outbreak has prompted international health organizations to mobilize resources.

Health workers on the ground are receiving support from aid agencies racing to contain the virus. The Ebola outbreak has spread across multiple areas of the country, straining local medical capacity and raising concerns about further transmission.

cards.headline: Tren de Aragua Gang Leader Killed in Joint US-Venezuela Strike
cards.teaser: Venezuelan and American officials confirmed that a gang leader wanted in the United States was killed in a joint military operation this week.
cards.body:
The United States military killed Hector Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, a leader of the Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua known as Niño Guerrero, in an airstrike this week. President Trump announced the operation on social media, describing it as a "swift and lethal kinetic strike" conducted at his direction by US Southern Command.

The operation represents a rare moment of security cooperation between Washington and Caracas, despite their historically tense diplomatic relations. Guerrero was wanted by American authorities and had been identified as a significant figure within the gang.

cards.headline: Pentagon Adds Alibaba, Baidu, and BYD to Chinese Military Company List
cards.teaser: The Defense Department designated three major Chinese technology and manufacturing firms as companies supporting the Chinese military.
cards.body:
The Pentagon updated its list of Chinese military companies to include Alibaba, Baidu, and BYD, three of China's largest technology and manufacturing firms. Alibaba operates major e-commerce platforms, Baidu provides internet search and AI technology, and BYD manufactures electric vehicles. The designation can restrict these companies' ability to conduct business with US entities and access American capital markets.

China's government expressed strong dissatisfaction with the Pentagon's decision. The updated list was released less than a month after Donald Trump met with Xi Jinping in Beijing, where the two leaders maintained a delicate trade war truce.

cards.headline: Falling Wages and Rising Wealth Deepen Economic Discontent
cards.teaser: Workers face declining purchasing power while asset values surge for wealthy Americans.
cards.body:
American workers are experiencing wage declines even as wealth concentrations reach new highs, contributing to economic dissatisfaction. The divergence between falling worker compensation and surging asset values has widened the gap between those who own substantial investments and those dependent on wages. Higher prices have eroded purchasing power for wage earners while stock and real estate values have climbed.

The wealth concentration coincided with Elon Musk becoming the first trillionaire following the SpaceX public offering. Workers also face uncertainty about artificial intelligence eliminating jobs, adding to economic anxiety despite low unemployment rates. The combination of wage pressure, inflation, and automation fears helps explain persistent negative sentiment about the economy among many Americans.

cards.headline: State attorneys general investigate OpenAI over data practices
cards.body:
OpenAI is under investigation by state attorneys general who are examining the company's advertising policies and how it handles health data. The specific states involved in the probe have not been publicly identified.

The investigation focuses on multiple aspects of OpenAI's operations, including its advertising practices and the management of health information collected through its services. State-level investigations of this kind can proceed independently of federal oversight and may ultimately result in enforcement actions, financial settlements, or requirements for the company to change how it operates.

OpenAI has increasingly drawn regulatory attention as its products have gained widespread adoption. The company operates ChatGPT and develops large language models that millions of people use globally. Regulators examining AI companies have placed particular emphasis on how these firms handle user data, especially sensitive categories like health information.

State attorneys general have become more engaged in regulating technology companies in recent years. Their focus has centered on consumer protection, data privacy, and advertising practices. These officials have the power to enforce state consumer protection laws and can pursue remedies ranging from financial penalties to mandatory changes in business practices.

The investigation reflects broader questions about how AI companies collect, store, and utilize user data. As these systems become more integrated into daily life and handle increasingly sensitive information, regulators have stepped up scrutiny of the industry's data management practices.

The full scope of the investigation and its expected timeline remain unclear. OpenAI has not made any public statements about the probe or confirmed whether it has received formal information requests from state officials.

This marks the latest regulatory challenge for OpenAI, which has faced mounting scrutiny from government agencies as artificial intelligence technology has become more prominent. The company's practices around data handling and advertising are now subjects of examination at the state level, where attorneys general have demonstrated a growing willingness to challenge major technology firms over consumer protection concerns.

The outcome of such investigations can vary considerably. Some result in quick settlements, while others lead to protracted legal disputes and significant changes to company operations. State-level actions can also prompt investigations by other state officials, potentially creating a coordinated multi-state effort to address shared concerns about a company's practices.

For OpenAI, this investigation adds to an already complex regulatory environment. The company faces questions about its data practices, business model, and the societal impact of its technology from multiple levels of government and regulatory bodies.

cards.headline: Resident doctors cancel planned strike after new government offer
cards.teaser: A walkout by resident doctors scheduled to begin Monday morning has been called off following a new offer from the government.
cards.body:
Resident doctors have called off a strike that was set to begin Monday at 07:00 BST and run through Friday. The cancellation followed a new offer presented by the government.

The decision prevents a week-long disruption to hospital services across the country.

hero.headline: Ukrainian Drone Strike Kills One in Southern Russia, Triggers Fire at Sea Terminal
hero.teaser: A Ukrainian drone attack on southern Russia killed one person and injured three others while setting a sea terminal ablaze.
hero.body:
A Ukrainian drone attack in southern Russia killed one person and wounded three others, Russian officials reported. The strike caused a fire at a sea terminal in the region.

Ukraine has intensified its campaign against Russian targets, striking energy infrastructure and military installations deep within Russian territory. These attacks represent an expansion of Ukraine's strategy to damage Russian assets far from active front-line combat.

cards.headline: Anthropic Suspends New AI Tools Over US Security Concerns
cards.teaser: The AI company paused its recently released Claude Fable 5 system after government officials raised cybersecurity and hacking concerns.
cards.body:
Anthropic has disabled its most advanced AI models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, following a US government export control directive. The company received orders to suspend access to these models for all foreign nationals due to national security concerns. Anthropic stated it would "abruptly disable" the tools for all users.

The US government cited concerns that safeguards in the models could be bypassed, potentially allowing them to be used to identify software vulnerabilities. Anthropic received the directive without being given specific details about the security threat.

cards.headline: Five Children Killed in Van and SUV Collision in Rural Ontario
cards.teaser: Four girls and one boy died when a van carrying 10 people collided with an SUV in Ontario, with an infant seriously injured.
cards.body:
Five children died in a collision between a van and an SUV in rural Ontario. The victims included four girls and one boy who were among 10 people traveling in the van at the time of the crash.

An infant was seriously injured in the accident, according to police. The collision occurred in a rural area of the province, though specific details about the cause of the crash were not provided by authorities.

cards.headline: Trump Name Removed from Kennedy Center Following Court Order
cards.teaser: Crews began work to remove President Trump's name from the Kennedy Center after a court mandated the change.
cards.body:
Workers began removing President Trump's name from the Kennedy Center's facade in the early hours of Saturday, shortly after a federal judge rejected an emergency appeal to block the removal. The Kennedy Center had missed a court-ordered deadline to remove "The Donald J Trump and" from the building's exterior by Friday at 11:59 p.m.

Crews had erected scaffolding on Friday as onlookers gathered to watch, but storms delayed the actual removal work until Saturday. The name removal followed a legal dispute over the naming rights to the prominent Washington cultural venue.

cards.headline: Canada Sees G7 Role in Potential Iran Agreement
cards.teaser: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said middle-power countries through the G7 could contribute to any US-Iran deal.
cards.body:
Mark Carney said the Group of Seven nations could play a role in any agreement between the United States and Iran. The Canadian prime minister made the comments ahead of an upcoming G7 meeting.

Carney argued that middle-power countries should not compete for favor with the United States but could meaningfully support diplomatic efforts. His remarks come as negotiations between Washington and Tehran appear to be nearing a conclusion.

hero.headline: Kennedy Center removes Trump name from building facade
hero.body:
Workers removed former President Donald Trump's name from the Kennedy Center's facade in the early hours of Saturday, following a federal judge's order and after the venue missed a Friday deadline to complete the task.

The removal came after US District Judge Christopher Cooper ruled that Trump's name must be taken down from the performing arts center in Washington DC. The work began shortly after 11:59pm Friday, when the deadline passed. An appeals court in Washington DC had rejected an emergency appeal filed by Justice Department lawyers on Friday seeking to pause the removal.

Judge Cooper's 94-page opinion stated that the Kennedy Center's founding statute makes clear the venue is named for President John F. Kennedy and cannot bear another formal name without congressional action. "Congress gave the Kennedy Center its name, and only Congress can change it," Cooper wrote. The ruling also temporarily blocked the venue from closing for renovations, stopping a two-year "revitalization project" that Trump's handpicked board had approved.

The facade previously read "The Donald J Trump and The John F Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts." Trump's name has now been fully removed from the building's exterior.

Before the physical removal, the Kennedy Center had already taken steps to comply with the court's broader order. The center's general counsel sent a memo to employees directing them to change email signatures, letterheads, and other documents to reflect the name "The John F Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts" or simply "Kennedy Center." Additional changes to templates, forms, signage, brochures, and website pages were required by June 12.

The removal of Trump's name from the website came days before that deadline, according to reports from the Washington Post.

Trump responded to the judge's decision with a lengthy statement on social media last month, saying he had no interest in what he called a "hopeless journey into NEVER NEVER LAND." The Justice Department's subsequent emergency appeal attempted to stay Cooper's removal order but was unsuccessful.

The Kennedy Center, which opened to the public in 1971, serves as the national performing arts center and the nation's cultural hub in Washington. Congress established it in 1958 as the National Cultural Center and renamed it to honor President Kennedy following his assassination in 1963. The venue hosts theatrical performances, concerts, and cultural events throughout the year while receiving federal funding alongside private donations and ticket sales.

cards.headline: Two detained after equipment stolen from England World Cup team vehicles
cards.teaser: Police are investigating the theft of equipment from England national team vehicles during their relocation to Kansas City for the World Cup.
cards.body:
Two people have been detained following a theft from England's national soccer team vehicles. The incident occurred as the team traveled from their pre-training base in Florida to Kansas City, their World Cup base camp.

England has since recovered their stolen boots. The team is competing in the World Cup tournament being held across multiple U.S. cities.

cards.headline: Empty seats visible at World Cup matches in Bay Area stadium
cards.teaser: FIFA blamed empty seats during a World Cup match on fans watching from concourses, as Levi's Stadium hosts tournament games months after the Super Bowl.
cards.body:
Numerous empty red seats have been visible at Levi's Stadium during World Cup matches in the Bay Area. FIFA addressed the issue following a match between South Korea and the Czech Republic, explaining that fans opted to watch from the stadium's concourses instead of sitting in their assigned seats.

Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara hosted the Super Bowl just four months before welcoming World Cup matches as part of the tournament's venues across the United States.

cards.headline: Resident doctors cancel planned strike after new government offer
cards.teaser: A walkout by resident doctors scheduled to begin Monday morning has been called off following a new offer from the government.
cards.body:
Resident doctors have called off a strike that was set to begin Monday at 07:00 BST and run through Friday. The cancellation followed a new offer presented by the government.

The decision prevents a week-long disruption to hospital services across the country.

cards.headline: Trump names James McDonald as US Attorney for Southern District of New York
cards.teaser: President Trump has selected James McDonald, a partner at Sullivan & Cromwell, to lead the powerful Manhattan federal prosecutor's office.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump announced his selection of James M. McDonald to serve as United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York. McDonald is currently a partner at the law firm Sullivan & Cromwell.

The Southern District of New York is one of the most influential federal prosecutor offices in the country, handling high-profile cases involving financial crimes, corruption, terrorism, and organized crime. Based in Manhattan, the office has jurisdiction over New York City and surrounding counties. McDonald will lead the office pending Senate confirmation.

cards.headline: Texas Republican leaders call for party unity at state convention
cards.teaser: Ken Paxton and other Texas Republican leaders urged party unity at the GOP convention as the state party platform draws attention.
cards.body:
The Guardian source is about a different story (an elephant at the Texas GOP convention), and the NPR source is completely unrelated (about a Scottish soccer fan). Neither provides verified information about the original news card's main claims regarding Ken Paxton, Greg Abbott's speech, Abraham George's reelection bid, or the platform discussions.

I'm returning the original card text unchanged:

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and other Republican leaders in the state called for party unity during speeches at the Texas GOP convention. The gathering brought together party members and officials to discuss platform positions and party direction.

Gregory Abbott also spoke at the convention, calling for a major election change during his address. The convention also saw Texas GOP Chair Abraham George lose his reelection bid. The Texas Republican Party platform has been described as becoming more extreme and influential in recent reporting.

cards.headline: Thousands attend anti-racism rally in Belfast following week of disorder
cards.teaser: Demonstrators gathered at Belfast City Hall for a rally against racism after a week of violence and disorder in the city.
cards.body:
Thousands of protesters gathered at Belfast City Hall to demonstrate against racism following a week of violence and disorder in the city. The rally represented a significant public response to the recent tensions that had gripped the community.

The turnout reflected widespread concern about the disturbances and a collective desire to stand against racism. Participants came together to show solidarity and voice their opposition to the prejudice that had contributed to the week's unrest.

hero.headline: US Restricts Foreign Access to Anthropic's Latest AI Models
hero.body:
The US government has ordered Anthropic to suspend access to its most advanced artificial intelligence models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, for all foreign nationals, the company announced. The directive came through an export control order citing national security concerns, though Anthropic said it was not given specific details about the security risks.

In response to the government order, Anthropic said it will "abruptly disable" these models for all users. The company had previously released Fable 5 to the public this week and was providing Mythos 5 to a limited group of companies including Apple and Goldman Sachs for testing purposes.

The timing of the restriction follows a series of security concerns about Mythos. Bloomberg reported that unauthorised users gained access to the model through a third-party contractor environment, raising alarms about how powerful AI technology could be protected from misuse. Anthropic confirmed it was investigating the breach claim.

Mythos has drawn particular attention from government authorities and international officials because of its potential to enable cybersecurity attacks. The UK's AI Security Institute warned that Mythos represents a "step up" from previous models in terms of the cyber-threat it poses. The institute said the model could carry out complex attacks requiring multiple steps and discover weaknesses in IT systems without human intervention, tasks that would normally take professionals days to complete.

The UK's AI minister, Kanishka Narayan, expressed concern about the model's ability to identify flaws in IT systems that hackers could exploit. Mythos was the first AI model to successfully complete a 32-step simulation of a cyber-attack created by the UK institute, solving it in three of ten attempts.

The restrictions mark a significant shift in Anthropic's global operations. The company had previously made its AI models available to users worldwide, but will now limit access to US-based users only. This decision affects how the company competes internationally against rivals like OpenAI and Google, which also operate advanced language models. By restricting Fable 5 and Mythos 5 to domestic users, Anthropic may lose international market share while attempting to comply with government guidance on AI access controls.

The move reflects broader government scrutiny of AI technology exports and foreign access to powerful American-developed systems. As artificial intelligence capabilities advance, US officials have expressed growing interest in controlling access to the most sophisticated models, particularly amid competition with other nations in AI development. Anthropic has not specified whether the restrictions are temporary or what conditions might allow foreign access to resume in the future.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO Creates 4,400 Employee Millionaires
cards.teaser: The company's public offering turned thousands of workers into millionaires through stock compensation.
cards.body:
SpaceX's initial public offering generated millionaire status for approximately 4,400 employees who held stock in the company. The historic IPO, which valued the space exploration company at record levels, converted employee stock grants and options into substantial wealth for workers across various roles, from engineers to welders.

One former SpaceX welder became a millionaire through shares accumulated during employment at the company. The public offering represents a major payday for employees who accepted stock compensation as part of their pay packages over the years. The offering marks one of the largest wealth creation events for rank-and-file employees in recent corporate history.

cards.headline: Elon Musk Retains Control Despite SpaceX Going Public
cards.teaser: The SpaceX founder structured the initial public offering to maintain nearly all decision-making power.
cards.body:
SpaceX has completed the largest IPO ever, listing on the Nasdaq with a valuation of $2.2 trillion. Musk structured the offering to maintain control over the company while raising capital from public markets through a dual-class share structure that gives him decisive power over major decisions.

The IPO marks a dramatic turnaround for a company Musk said had "less than a 10% chance of succeeding" at its founding. Musk's net worth has reached $1.11 trillion according to the Bloomberg rich list, making him the world's first trillionaire. Investors are backing Musk's space exploration and satellite internet vision despite having minimal influence over corporate governance.

cards.headline: Stock Market Holds Steady Following SpaceX Public Debut
cards.teaser: Markets absorbed the record-sized initial public offering without major disruption.
cards.body:
Financial markets remained stable as SpaceX completed its initial public offering on the Nasdaq stock exchange, raising $75 billion in a record-breaking debut. The company achieved a valuation of $2.1 trillion following its first day of public trading.

Elon Musk's personal wealth reached $1.1 trillion, making him the world's first trillionaire. His net worth increased by more than $62 billion as a result of the SpaceX IPO, according to Forbes.

cards.headline: Study Links Remote Work to Increased Loneliness and Mental Health Concerns
cards.teaser: Research suggests working from home carries social and psychological costs for employees.
cards.body:
A new study found that remote work contributes to increased loneliness and worsening mental health among employees. The research challenges the assumption that worker preference for remote arrangements automatically translates to better wellbeing outcomes. Employees reported higher satisfaction with work-from-home flexibility but experienced negative effects on social connection and mental state.

The findings add complexity to ongoing debates about office requirements and remote work policies. While workers consistently express preference for remote options, the study suggests these arrangements may have hidden costs related to isolation and reduced social interaction. The research has implications for companies weighing return-to-office mandates against employee demands for continued remote work flexibility.

cards.headline: Amazon CEO raised concerns about Anthropic models before government action
cards.teaser: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy may have been the source of security concerns that led to government action against Anthropic.
cards.body:
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy reportedly raised security concerns about Anthropic's AI models before the government directed the company to restrict access on Friday. The concerns allegedly led Anthropic to cut off worldwide access to two of its models.

The connection between Jassy's reported warnings and the subsequent government crackdown suggests coordination between the private sector and regulators on AI safety issues. Anthropic, which counts Amazon among its major investors, complied with the directive to suspend global access to the models in question.

cards.headline: KPMG withdraws report on AI usage after apparent hallucinations
cards.teaser: The consulting firm pulled a report on artificial intelligence after the document appeared to contain AI-generated errors.
cards.body:
KPMG has withdrawn a report about AI usage after discovering what appear to be hallucinations in the document. The incident highlights ongoing reliability issues with AI-generated content, even in professional settings.

The withdrawal represents an example of AI systems producing inaccurate information about their own technology sector. KPMG has not specified which portions of the report contained errors or how the hallucinated content made it through the firm's review process before publication.

cards.headline: NASA revises Artemis lunar lander plans
cards.teaser: NASA is reshaping its approach to lunar lander development for the Artemis program.
cards.body:
NASA has adjusted its plans for the Artemis lunar lander as development continues toward the Artemis III mission. The agency has also announced crew members for the Artemis program, though these named astronauts will not be landing on the Moon or traveling there for this mission phase.

The revised lander approach reflects NASA's ongoing work to develop the hardware and systems needed to support the mission's goal of returning astronauts to the lunar surface.

cards.headline: FBI creates replica town to simulate cyberattacks
cards.teaser: The bureau built a full-scale mock town inside an Alabama facility to train agents on cyber threats.
cards.body:
The FBI has built a replica small town inside a building in Alabama to serve as a training facility for simulating cyberattacks. This dedicated cyber training ground allows agents to practice responding to digital threats in a realistic environment that mirrors actual infrastructure and systems found in real communities.

The facility provides a controlled space where the FBI can test defensive strategies and prepare personnel for scenarios involving attacks on critical infrastructure, reflecting the agency's commitment to addressing the growing threat of cyber warfare and digital attacks on civilian systems.

cards.headline: Researchers measure global length of underground fungal networks
cards.teaser: Scientists have calculated that fungal networks stretch far enough to reach beyond the solar system.
cards.body:
Researchers have quantified the length and mass of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal networks on a global scale, finding the total length extends beyond the solar system. The measurements provide new insight into the scale of these underground ecosystems that connect plant roots.

Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi form symbiotic relationships with plants, creating vast underground networks that facilitate nutrient exchange. The research demonstrates the enormous scope of these biological systems that play a role in nutrient cycling and plant health across terrestrial ecosystems worldwide.

cards.headline: iOS 27 adds features to Apple Wallet
cards.teaser: Apple's upcoming operating system will make switching between payment cards easier and add digital pass creation.
cards.body:
iOS 27 will introduce several new features to Apple Wallet. The update makes it easier to switch between Apple Pay cards, streamlining the payment experience for iPhone users.

The software also enables users to create digital versions of physical credentials and cards through a new Create a Pass feature. These changes expand Wallet's functionality as Apple continues positioning it as a comprehensive replacement for physical cards and identification documents.

hero.headline: Qatar earns first World Cup point with late equalizer against Switzerland
hero.body:
Qatar secured their first point in World Cup history after Boualem Khoukhi scored a stoppage-time equalizer to draw 1-1 with Switzerland in San Francisco. The goal marked a historic moment for the Gulf nation in their Group B match.

Switzerland appeared set to claim all three points before Khoukhi's late intervention denied them victory. The result gives Qatar their first point across all World Cup appearances, after failing to win a single match in their previous tournament as hosts.

The match took place at one of the 2026 World Cup venues in San Francisco, where the expanded tournament is being co-hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico. The Group B standings remain tight as both teams look to advance from the opening round.

For Switzerland, the draw represents two points dropped after controlling much of the match. They will need to regroup for their remaining group matches to secure passage to the knockout stages. Qatar, meanwhile, will take significant confidence from their first World Cup point, demonstrating improvement from their previous tournament showing.

The 2026 World Cup features 48 teams for the first time, up from 32 in previous editions. The expanded format gives more nations like Qatar additional opportunities to compete on the global stage and build experience at the highest level of international football.

cards.headline: West Indies defeats defending champion New Zealand in close finish
cards.teaser: Shemaine Campbelle's unbeaten 90 guides West Indies past New Zealand with one ball remaining.
cards.body:
Shemaine Campbelle's unbeaten 90 guided West Indies to a thrilling victory over defending champions New Zealand. The West Indies secured the win with just one ball remaining in a tense match.

The result marks an impressive triumph for West Indies against the reigning champions, with Campbelle's decisive innings proving crucial in the narrow victory.

cards.headline: England's Littler and Humphries advance to World Cup of Darts quarterfinals
cards.teaser: The English pair defeated Spain's Cristo Reyes and Jose Justicia 8-5 to set up a match against Wales.
cards.body:
Luke Humphries and Luke Littler secured England's passage to the World Cup of Darts quarterfinals with an 8-5 victory over Spain's Cristo Reyes and Jose Justicia.

The English pair will now face Wales in the next round of the competition.

cards.headline: Emma Raducanu reaches Queen's final with two wins in one day
cards.teaser: Raducanu won twice on Saturday to advance to the final, while Katie Boulter lost her semifinal match.
cards.body:
Emma Raducanu reached the Queen's Club final by winning two matches in a single day, despite an early scare when she slipped on the grass and hurt her left thigh. She recovered to deliver a dominant performance against 18-year-old Iva Jovic, winning 6-2, 6-2 in front of a supportive home crowd.

Raducanu will face Donna Vekic in the final as she continues her grass court preparation. Fellow British player Katie Boulter was eliminated in her semifinal match.

cards.headline: Four Iran World Cup staff win visa appeals, 11 remain barred from US
cards.teaser: Members of Iran's delegation successfully appealed visa rejections, but most staff still cannot travel to the United States.
cards.body:
Four members of Iran's World Cup delegation have successfully appealed their visa rejections and won approval to travel to the United States. However, 11 other staff members remain banned from entering the country.

The visa decisions affect Iran's support staff as the team competes in the tournament. The 11 staff members who were denied will be unable to join the delegation for matches held on American soil.

cards.headline: Arsenal and Liverpool pursue PSG winger Bradley Barcola
cards.teaser: Both Premier League clubs are among the suitors for the Paris Saint-Germain forward.
cards.body:
Arsenal and Liverpool are among the clubs pursuing Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, with the winger drawing attention from multiple suitors during the transfer window.

Elsewhere in the transfer market, Brighton have rejected a bid from Coventry for goalkeeper Carl Rushworth. Bayern Munich are also in contention to sign Marcus Rashford, potentially ahead of Barcelona in the race for the Manchester United forward.

cards.headline: Exeter reaches Premiership final after turnaround season
cards.teaser: Rob Baxter calls his team's rise from their worst season to a final one of his greatest achievements.
cards.body:
Exeter Chiefs reached the Premiership final after a stunning semi-final comeback against Bath, winning 27-26 in last-ditch drama. The away victory marked the first playoff win by a visiting team since Harlequins' famous comeback at Bristol in 2021.

The triumph capped a remarkable turnaround for Exeter, who bounced back from their poorest season on record. Head coach Rob Baxter described the transformation as one of his greatest accomplishments, noting that while his squad comprises the same players, they have evolved into different competitors. Exeter will face Northampton at Twickenham for the Premiership title on Saturday.

hero.headline: Tyra Banks Sues Netflix Over Americas Next Top Model Documentary
hero.body:
Tyra Banks filed a lawsuit against Netflix on Saturday, alleging the streaming service manipulated her testimony in its recent documentary series Reality Check: Inside America's Next Top Model. The lawsuit claims defamation and accuses the platform of editing her interview in ways that misrepresented her statements and positions.

The suit names Netflix, 89 Blocks Holdings, EverWonder Studio, Netflix Music, and co-directors Mor Loushy and Daniel Sivan as defendants. Banks is pursuing claims for false light, defamation by implication, breach of contract, and false endorsement. According to the filing, her participation was used in ways that violated the terms under which she agreed to be interviewed.

Banks created and hosted America's Next Top Model, which ran from 2003 to 2018 and became a defining force in reality television. The show launched modeling careers and influenced fashion competition programming for years. Netflix's documentary examined the series and its impact through interviews with former contestants and figures connected to the production.

The heart of the lawsuit concerns how Banks' words were presented in the final documentary. According to the filing, the editing created false implications that harm her reputation. Banks states that viewers received a misleading impression of her statements regarding the show and its controversies.

According to the documentary's directors, Banks was given no advance questions, no approval over her presentation, and could only watch the finished series when it premiered publicly. "She had no say, no influence, no anything," co-director Mor Loushy told Vanity Fair. The directors said Banks agreed to participate so she could tell her side of the story and express her intentions to make modeling more inclusive.

The documentary has been a major success for Netflix, drawing over 14 million views in its first week and topping the platform's English-language charts. However, the series sparked significant criticism from former contestants and judges, many of whom felt Banks failed to take adequate responsibility for the show's toxic elements, including body-shaming and poor duty of care.

During the documentary, Banks acknowledged going "too far" with a famous confrontation with contestant Tiffany Richardson in cycle four, saying "You know, I lost it." However, former judges and contestants expressed frustration with what they viewed as insufficient accountability. Former judge Jay Manuel said Banks was not "willing to be a little more vulnerable" and that viewers saw "Television Tyra" rather than genuine remorse.

The lawsuit raises important questions about documentary editing practices and the responsibilities filmmakers have toward interview subjects. Banks seeks damages for what she describes as harm to her professional reputation and violations of her participation agreement.

Netflix has not publicly responded to the lawsuit. The case represents a significant legal challenge for the streaming platform and the documentary's production team.

cards.headline: Michael Biopic Becomes Highest-Grossing Music Film Ever
cards.teaser: The Michael Jackson biopic has earned more than any other music biography film in history.
cards.body:
The biopic about Michael Jackson has become the highest-grossing music biography film of all time. The movie brought in $911.9 million worldwide, surpassing the previous record holder Bohemian Rhapsody.

The film stars Colman Domingo and has been in theaters since earlier this year. The box office performance marks a significant milestone for music biographical films and reflects sustained audience interest in Jackson's life and career.

cards.headline: Trump Name Removed From Kennedy Center After Court Order
cards.teaser: Workers removed Donald Trump's name from the performing arts venue's exterior following a court deadline.
cards.body:
Donald Trump's name was removed from the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington DC early Saturday morning, hours after a federal judge rejected an emergency appeal to block the removal. The venue had missed a court-ordered deadline to remove "The Donald J Trump and" from its facade by Friday at 11:59pm.

Work began in the early hours of Saturday with crews erecting scaffolding to complete the task. The removal followed legal action initiated against the performing arts venue regarding the president's name displayed on the building's exterior.

cards.headline: Wanda Sykes Says Bill Maher Confronted Her Over Golden Globes Joke
cards.teaser: The comedian said the talk show host approached her after she made a joke about him while presenting at the awards ceremony.
cards.body:
Wanda Sykes said Bill Maher confronted her after she made a joke about him during the Golden Globes ceremony in January. While presenting the award for best performance in stand-up comedy, Sykes joked about facing criticism as a queer Black woman doing the job of two mediocre white guys.

Sykes said the remark was clearly intended as a joke. Maher, who hosts a late-night talk show, approached Sykes about the comment after the awards ceremony. Sykes shared the details of the encounter during a recent interview.

cards.headline: Amy Adams Declined SNL Sketch to Protect Young Enchanted Fans
cards.teaser: The actress said she turned down a graphic sketch idea from Andy Samberg while hosting Saturday Night Live in 2008.
cards.body:
Amy Adams turned down a sketch idea while hosting Saturday Night Live in 2008 because she felt it was too graphic for younger viewers. Andy Samberg had pitched the concept, but Adams declined to participate.

Adams explained her decision during an appearance on Late Night With Seth Meyers, noting that she wanted to protect the young girls watching who knew her from the Disney film Enchanted. The hosting gig came just four months after the fairytale comedy premiered in theaters.

cards.headline: Colman Domingo Discusses Working With Spielberg on Disclosure Day
cards.teaser: The actor spoke about his role in Steven Spielberg's new film and his views on extraterrestrial life.
cards.body:
Colman Domingo discussed working with director Steven Spielberg on the film Disclosure Day and shared his thoughts on the possibility of alien life. The actor said he believes in extraterrestrial life, stating it cannot just be humans in the universe.

Domingo plays a character named Hugo in Spielberg's film. The actor has appeared in multiple projects this year, including the Michael Jackson biopic Michael and the final season of Euphoria. He also stars in and directed an episode of Netflix's The Four Seasons.

cards.headline: Keke Palmer and Sean Evans Seen Together in New York
cards.teaser: The actress and the Hot Ones host were spotted on what appeared to be a date in New York City.
cards.body:
Keke Palmer and Sean Evans were spotted together in New York City on what appeared to be a date, according to reports. The sighting has sparked speculation about a potential romantic connection between the two personalities.

Evans is known for hosting the popular YouTube series Hot Ones, which features celebrities answering interview questions while eating progressively spicier chicken wings. Palmer is an actress and television personality with an extensive career in film and television.

hero.headline: White House to sign framework for Iran peace deal Sunday
hero.body:
President Trump announced Saturday that the United States plans to sign a peace framework with Iran on Sunday, capping weeks of negotiations between the two countries. The announcement comes as the administration seeks to reshape relations with Tehran after years of tension between Washington and the Iranian government.

Trump wrote on Truth Social that the deal is scheduled to be signed and described the current relationship with Iran as better than what previous administrations achieved. He expressed hope that the process will work out successfully. The framework represents a significant shift in US policy toward Iran, though specific details of the agreement have not been disclosed publicly.

The impending deal has drawn criticism from some Democrats in Congress. Representative Seth Moulton of Massachusetts called the reported terms a terrible deal and characterized it as a surrender document from Trump to Iran's supreme leader. His comments on MS NOW reflected concerns among some lawmakers about the substance of the negotiations and what concessions may have been made to reach an agreement.

Interior Secretary Doug Burgum defended the administration's approach to Iran on Friday, though he focused his remarks on domestic energy policy rather than the diplomatic negotiations. The signing comes at a time when gas prices have become a point of political contention, with Burgum attributing price variations to state policies rather than international factors.

The Iran framework marks one of the most significant foreign policy developments of Trump's current term. The Sunday signing will formalize a new direction in US-Iran relations, though the agreement will likely face scrutiny from Congress and require implementation steps before its full impact becomes clear. The deal stands in contrast to the Obama-era nuclear agreement, which Trump has criticized repeatedly.

cards.headline: Amazon prompted White House to shut down Anthropic's Fable AI model
cards.teaser: Anthropic's Fable 5 AI model was removed from public access days after launch following an urgent report from Amazon to the White House.
cards.body:
An urgent report from Amazon triggered a White House response that led to the removal of Anthropic's Fable 5 AI model from public access on Friday night. The powerful AI system had been available to the public for only a few days before the takedown.

The incident raises questions about Amazon's role in the decision, given that the company is a major investor in Anthropic. The episode has drawn attention to how the administration and industry respond to rapidly advancing AI technology on a reactive basis.

cards.headline: Democrat Moulton calls Iran peace deal a surrender document
cards.teaser: Representative Seth Moulton criticized the reported terms of the US-Iran agreement ahead of Sunday's planned signing.
cards.body:
Democratic Representative Seth Moulton of Massachusetts sharply criticized the reported details of the Iran peace framework on Saturday, calling it a terrible deal. He told MS NOW that the agreement amounts to a surrender document from President Trump to Iran's supreme leader.

Moulton's comments reflect concerns among some lawmakers about the substance of the negotiations with Iran. The criticism comes one day before the White House plans to sign the peace framework, which Trump has described as representing a better relationship with Tehran than previous administrations achieved.

cards.headline: Cruz backs candidates opposing Trump endorsements in Georgia, South Carolina
cards.teaser: Senator Ted Cruz is supporting candidates in two governor races who are running against Trump-endorsed Republicans.
cards.body:
Texas Senator Ted Cruz announced this week that he is backing Rick Jackson for Georgia governor and Alan Wilson for South Carolina governor. Both candidates are running against Trump-endorsed Republicans in their respective primary races.

The endorsements represent a break from the president as Cruz positions himself ahead of a potential 2028 presidential campaign. Cruz is testing whether the Republican Party has room for a White House contender willing to diverge from Trump, who has maintained control over the party for the past decade.

cards.headline: Trump endorsement complicates Hilton's California governor campaign
cards.teaser: GOP nominee Steve Hilton faces challenges running as a Trump-endorsed candidate in a state where the president is unpopular.
cards.body:
President Trump's voter fraud accusations in California have created difficulties for gubernatorial nominee Steve Hilton, who is navigating a campaign as a Trump-endorsed Republican in a state where the president faces significant disapproval. Hilton, a British political adviser turned US politician, has promoted his Trump endorsement throughout the race.

The situation illustrates the balancing act facing Republican candidates in blue states who seek Trump's backing. While the endorsement is considered the most valuable in GOP politics nationally, it presents unique challenges in California, where Trump's popularity remains low among the broader electorate.

cards.headline: Burgum attributes gas price variations to state policy, not Iran tensions
cards.teaser: The Interior Secretary said gasoline prices differ across the country primarily due to state taxes and policies.
cards.body:
Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said Friday that gasoline price differences across the United States result primarily from state policy and taxes rather than underlying market fundamentals. He made the comments to Fox News amid rising gas prices during tensions in the Strait of Hormuz region related to Iran.

Burgum pointed to several states' policies when discussing price variations around the country. His remarks shift attention from international factors to domestic state-level decisions as the main driver of regional gas price differences.

cards.headline: Iranian ambassador suggests US friendship possible if Israel ties reduced
cards.teaser: Iran's envoy to Mexico said the two countries could have good relations if the US does not take foreign policy direction from Israel.
cards.body:
Iran's ambassador to Mexico said Friday that his country and the United States could develop a good relationship if President Trump does not base foreign policy decisions on Israel's interests. Ambassador Abolfazl Pasandjdeh told reporters that Iran and the US can be very good friends if the US closes its eyes to Israel's interest.

The comments come one day before the planned signing of a peace framework between Washington and Tehran. The ambassador's remarks highlight the role of Israel in Iranian calculations about relations with the United States.
